newsitem.title: USA: Lower grain, milk prices depress U.S. farm index.
newsitem.headline: Lower grain, milk prices depress U.S. farm index.

text.p: Falling prices for corn, wheat, soybeans, milk and oranges helped spark a 1.8 percent decline in the farm price index in November, the Agriculture Department said Wednesday.
The index is a guage of prices paid to farmers for their crops and livestock. For November, the index stood at 110, down two points from October but four points higher than a year ago.
Prices for lettuce, cattle, eggs and grapes rose in November.
The abundant fall harvest helped depress grain and oilseed prices. Farmers were forecast to reap the second largest soybean crop and third largest corn crop on record.
Corn prices fell by 25 cents a bushel from October to average $2.64, which was 23 cents a bushel lower than a year earlier.
Soybeans sold for an average $6.80 per bushel, down 15 cents from October. One year ago, the price was $6.40.
At $4.07 per bushel, the wheat price was down 11 cents from the previous month and 74 cents lower than November 1995.
Larger-than-expected milk output in November helped reduce the milk price to $15.20 per 100 pounds, down 90 cents from October but still $1.20 higher than one year ago.
Cattle prices rose during November to average $64.80 per 100 pounds, up $1.70 from October and $4.10 from one year ago.
Hog prices fell to $54.40 per 100 pounds, down $1.20 from October but $14.50 higher than November 1995.

Oranges averaged $4.07 per box, nearly half of October's $8.62 a box. Lettuce sold for an average $23.70 per 100 pounds, compared with $15.50 in October. At $1,430 per ton, grapes were up $210 from October.
Cotton prices averaged 70.9 cents per pound, down 0.6 cents from October and 4.1 cents lower than one year ago.
